subject: Is there any way to pass input parameters to a shiny app on startup?

messages.author: ec53b50a5511d439
messages.subject: Is there any way to pass input parameters to a shiny app on startup?
parts:
Hi all,

I've built a function that at a certain point executes runApp(). Now, I want to be able to pass a couple of input parameters to the function, and want these to be passed on to the shiny app. So running the following command:

myfun(a=1,b=2)

...would result in the following statement being run within the function:

[...]
runApp("myapp")
[...]

And from within the shiny app, i.e. in server.R, I would then want to access the values a and b.

Is there any way to do this? Can I somehow pass the parameters a and b as a list of input parameters to runApp()? Or is the recommended practice to try to access the namespace of myfun()?

I haven't managed to find any answer to this by searching the forum, but if this question's already been answered I'd be grateful if anyone could point me in the right direction :)

Thanks in advance,
Love Hansson

messages.author: 9711d30301c32133
messages.subject: Re: Is there any way to pass input parameters to a shiny app on startup?
parts:
If you're embedding runApp() in a larger workflow, you may find this example helpful: https://gist.github.com/trestletech/5948876#file-server-r-L7 . It demonstrates the pattern of assigning a variable outside of a Shiny app then referencing that variable within Shiny.

The "parent" markdown file ("ReconstructGRN.Rmd") is the one that would be executed by the user. It calls "runApp" to run the Shiny application included in the gist. You can see that the Shiny App checks for the existence of the variable "gn" (on the highlighted line in server.R). This variable wasn't ever defined in the Shiny app -- only the parent markdown file.

Jeff
